entries.name: The Cult Cross
entries.content:
Everywhere Eden’s Gate went, they left their mark – a distinctive cross with two shorter crossbars (one above and one below the intersection). This Eden’s Gate cross became the emblem of Joseph Seed’s church. It flew on white flags outside captured locations, was painted on barn roofs and water towers, and even branded onto livestock and people to signify belonging to the cult. The design is reminiscent of a traditional Christian cross, but with subtle differences.

Each region had its own color scheme for the logo: Joseph kept a stark black cross on white for his compound, John favored a white cross on black (bold contrast, like the word “YES” on the hillside)​ and Faith’s areas often showed a black cross on a pale, mint-green background (the color of Bliss)​

To cult members, this symbol meant unity, faith, and protection; to non-cult locals, it quickly came to mean “you’re in Peggie territory – beware.”

entries.name: “YES” and Other Words
entries.content:
John Seed’s signature propaganda was the word “YES” spelled out in gigantic letters on a mountainside, visible across Holland Valley. He said “Yes” symbolized surrendering to God’s will (and to the cult) – “the Power of Yes,” as he called it​

 The cult also painted “SINNER” on properties of those marked for confession, “REPENT” on roads leading to their churches, and ominous messages like “THE END IS NIGH” on billboards (overwriting normal ads). Joseph’s preachings provided many catchphrases that got turned into graffiti: e.g., “Walk the Path”, “Embrace The Collapse”, “Reap Now, Rest Later.” These were scrawled on walls, vehicles, even carved into trees. The idea was to create an inescapable environment of cult messaging, so even if you avoided cult members, their words and symbols would still assail you psychologically.

entries.name: The Father’s Statue
entries.content: On a high promontory overlooking the Henbane River, the cult built a massive statue of Joseph Seed. This golden statue depicted Joseph in a Messiah-like pose, arms extended as if offering a hug or blessing. It closely resembled Christ the Redeemer statue in silhouette – undoubtedly intentional. Pilgrims from within the cult would make journeys to this statue, praying at its base. Inside the statue pedestal was a hidden chamber functioning as a Bliss production site and armory.

entries.name: Music and Broadcasts
entries.content: Eden’s Gate spread its influence through media as well. They hijacked the county radio station, K-OKA, replacing classic rock and country music with their own choral hymns and Joseph’s sermons. Songs like “Oh the Bliss” and “Keep Your Rifle by Your Side” – original cult compositions – became the soundtrack of occupied Hope County, echoing from radios and loudspeakers on cult trucks. Joseph also made heavy use of loudspeaker trucks: vehicles mounted with PA systems that would drive around broadcasting his pre-recorded speeches. Hearing Joseph’s calm voice crackling through a distant loudspeaker on a foggy morning could send chills down a hiding resident’s spine. In contrast, the Resistance would sometimes blast rebellious music

entries.name: Rituals and Ceremonies
entries.content: Symbolism extended to cult rituals which were essentially theater to reinforce belief. For example, baptisms (which we detail separately) were done in rivers under large hanging Eden’s Gate banners. Weddings within the cult – yes, some cult members got married during all this – were officiated by Joseph or Faith, and the couples would wear crowns of Bliss flowers (a symbol of giving their union to Eden’s Gate). The cult minted its own challenge coins and seals – Jacob had a “Challenge Coin” he gave to those who proved themselves strong (one side bearing the cross, the other a snarling wolf head). John gave out “Yes” pins to those who confessed (almost like a graduation badge). All these little symbols and tokens made members feel part of something and served as rewards, strengthening loyalty.

entries.name: Tattoos and Scars
entries.content:
Eden’s Gate members often bore physical marks. Many had tattoos of the Eden’s Gate cross on their bodies. John Seed took this further by carving sins into people​

Those carvings (wrath, greed, lust, etc., in Latin or English) became marks of shame turned redemption – after surviving John’s “atonement,” converts wore their scar as proof of being cleansed. John himself was covered in tattoos of the seven deadly sins over his torso (rumor has it each time he forced someone to confess, he’d tattoo that person’s sin onto himself too, as a weird burden-sharing). This extreme body modification culture in the cult meant you could sometimes identify a member by such scars or ink. In Hope County post-cult, those who were freed from Eden’s Gate carry these marks forever, a reminder on their very skin of what they endured.

entries.name: Vehicles and Colors
entries.content: The cult’s vehicles were painted white with black accents – a reversal of the typical military camo, almost saying “we’re not hiding, we’re claiming territory.” Most would have the Eden’s Gate cross painted on hood or side. Some special vehicles had names: Joseph’s personal pickup truck, “The Chariot,” had a custom license plate “YES4GOD”. John drove a red helicopter named “The Word” that he used to spray Bliss (it had loudspeakers to call out sinners). Faith had a boat called “Miracle” used to spread Bliss on the river. By branding everything from trucks to tiny prayer pamphlets with symbols and messages, the cult created an ecosystem of propaganda. For a time, it truly felt like Eden’s Gate was everywhere – visually, audibly, and spiritually – which was exactly Joseph’s intent: an all-encompassing symbolic takeover preceding the literal one.

entries.name: The Cleansing (Forced Baptisms)
entries.content:
The Cleansing (Forced Baptisms): One of John Seed’s most notorious practices was the forced baptism or “cleansing” ritual. Eden’s Gate believes everyone must confess their sins and be reborn; baptism is the physical act of that rebirth. But John didn’t wait for volunteers – his men would capture holdouts and bring them to water by force. In Holland Valley, they often used a specific site: a shallow ditch or makeshift baptismal pool near the Falls End Church or at the Silver Lake boathouse. There, under John’s direction, multiple cultists would hold a victim down in the water until they were on the verge of drowning​

They would shout at the thrashing person to “Let go! Say YES!” The symbolism is clear: nearly drowning = “dying” as a sinner, being lifted out = “born again” as cult. Many did not survive these drownings – those were written off as unworthy. Those who did, sputtering and finally crying “Yes… I will join,” were pulled up and surrounded by cheering cultists who welcomed them “into Eden.” It’s a horrific perversion of a holy sacrament. The Deputy endured this Cleansing ritual during one capture, and barely survived thanks to an interruption, making it a well-known event recounted among the Resistance.

entries.name: The Confession (John’s Interrogation)
entries.content: After the cleansing usually came confession. John Seed believed one must verbally confess their deepest sin. In practice, he would torture people until they confessed to something, anything, often in a chapel or bunker he called The Confession. He preferred psychological torment – tying someone to a chair under a bright light, playing his “Yes” propaganda video on loop​ or bringing in their loved ones and threatening them. John kept an ornate wooden Confessional (like in Catholic churches) but instead of listening to your sins, he’d drag you out of it and carve your sin on your flesh once you admitted it. He had an uncanny ability to dig out what someone was ashamed of most – greed, anger, etc. Many Resistance fighters have scars of these confessions. The process was deeply personal and traumatic, tailored to each victim’s psyche.

entries.name: The Atonement (Culmination)
entries.content:
In John’s doctrine, after confession comes atonement. That could mean various things: for some, John demanded they perform a violent act to prove their devotion (e.g., he handed a newly “cleansed” cultist a gun and ordered them to shoot a former friend who resisted – if they did it, they atoned in his eyes). For others, atonement was simpler: bearing the pain of the carving and baptism was itself atonement – surviving it meant you paid for your sin. For the particularly stubborn or “wretched,” John reserved a final step: The Wrath. He would literally flay the sin from your body. The chunks of skin he carved with the sin word? If he felt you still harbored that sin, he’d cut it off. 

He considered that the ultimate purging – “The Lord purged the sin from your flesh.” It’s unspeakably cruel, but John performed it with ritualistic zeal. He kept the strips of skin pinned on the walls of his bunker, labeled with the sins – a morbid tapestry of atonement.

entries.name: Faith’s “Cleansing”
entries.content: While John used torture and water, Faith Seed had a softer approach to forced confession. She’d give sinners a “choice” under Bliss. For instance, she drugged Marshal Burke so heavily that he willingly offered a false confession, screaming about his sins in a hallucination, then she bade him to “atone” by attacking his friends (which led to Virgil’s death). Faith’s method was to create a vivid hallucination where the person experiences their sins (guilt trip nightmares) and then appears to be “forgiven” by a vision of Faith/Joseph if they submit. It was a psychological baptism of sorts, entirely in one’s mind. Some folks exposed to Bliss recall apologizing to imagined figures from their past while Faith watched smiling. If they emerged docile, Faith considered them cleansed. If not, they either went insane or became one of her Angels.

entries.name: “Walk the Path” Ritual
entries.content: oseph had a ritual for his most devoted (and for those he particularly sought to convert). He’d have them walk a path through the woods, under the influence of Bliss or scripture, confronting symbolic trials (like visions of loved ones or temptations). At the end of the path, Joseph would be waiting in a clearing. There, the person was expected to either accept Joseph’s teachings fully or face death. This wasn’t done for most recruits – it was more for inner circle or special cases. It’s all very metaphorical, but in-universe it’s spoken of with reverence: “Only those who Walk the Path will reach Eden’s Gate.” It basically means those who go through all of the cult’s trials (cleansing, confession, atonement) and still keep faith are the ones considered true family.

entries.name: The Father’s Sermons and Teachings
entries.content:
Voice of a Prophet: Joseph Seed’s sermons are central to Eden’s Gate’s draw. He speaks calmly, often starting softly and building in intensity. He quotes liberally from the Book of Revelation and other apocalyptic scriptures, blending them with his own prophecies. A typical Joseph sermon might begin: “I know you are hurtin’. I know you are lost. But pain is a door. And through that door… is Eden.” He has an uncanny way of making listeners feel understood in their suffering, then offering his cult as the solution. Many joined simply because Joseph’s words gave them hope or a sense of purpose that modern life didn’t.
Core Messages: The central theme is that the Collapse is coming, a great cleansing fire that will purify the world​

. Joseph preaches that society is corrupt (pointing to examples like “bankers stealing from you, governments lying, neighbors betraying neighbors”), and that God chose him to save the righteous. He refers to Biblical floods and plagues, saying this time it will be nuclear fire. 

Phrases often heard:
“The path to Eden is clear to those who have faith.”​

“Collapse is upon us, and the reaping has begun… but do not fear, for God’s not forsaken you.”​

“We will walk through the gates of Eden, together.”

“Hear the word, feel the light, know that you are not alone.” (often said to comfort followers)

Sin and Salvation: Joseph teaches that every person is born a sinner (very much standard Christian doctrine), but he adds that sin has multiplied due to modern “poisons” like technology, immorality in media, etc. Only by suffering can one atone. “To be cleansed, you must feel the fire.” This is how he justifies the cult’s harsh methods; he frames it as tough love mandated by God. He also emphasizes family – calling all followers his children, and himself “the Father”. This paternal rhetoric makes devotees feel loved and part of a divine family, especially those who were lonely or without strong family ties before.

The Parables of Joseph: Throughout the conflict,
The Father’s Sermons: Joseph Seed’s preaching is mesmerizing and fearsome. He often begins softly: “We are all sinners. Every one of us… But God forgives those who have faith.” Then he crescendos into fire-and-brimstone prophecies. A recurring theme is that “the Collapse is upon us, and the reaping has begun… but there is nothing to fear” if you embrace Eden’s Gat​e. He speaks of Biblical plagues and modern vices in one breath, condemning the “sickness” of the modern world. Joseph invokes imagery from Revelation – rivers turning to blood, skies of fire – and positions himself as the shepherd to lead his flock through this coming wrath. “The path to Eden is clear to those who have faith,” he proclaims, promising salvation amidst destruction.
His sermons frequently reference sacrifice: “Every painful event is God testing us, refining us, preparing us for Eden.” To the faithful, his words are gospel that fortify them against doubt. To outsiders, his sermons are a chilling call for apocalypse. The Resistance members recall hearing Joseph’s broadcasts where he’d calmly list society’s sins – greed, immorality, atheism – and then calmly insist “I will protect you from the Collapse, but you must give yourself over fully.” This blend of doom and hope made his speeches both terrifying and strangely reassuring to listeners who felt lost. Even captured resistance fighters admitted that hearing Joseph speak face-to-face was disarming; he’d look into their eyes and talk about their personal pain or loss with uncanny empathy, then pivot to why joining him would free them from that pain. It’s cult indoctrination 101, delivered by a master orator. Every sermon bolstered the cult’s fanaticism – Joseph’s voice on the radio could spur a whole platoon of cultists to charge into gunfire fearlessly.

entries.name: “Only You” – Jacob’s Mind Control Trigger
entries.content:
Musical Brainwashing: Among the more bizarre cult mechanics was Jacob Seed’s use of the song “Only You” by The Platters as a mind-control trigger. Jacob, drawing on his military background in psychological warfare, conditioned certain people (including one of the Deputy’s fellow officers) to respond to this oldie tun​e. He’d captives endure torture and starvation while repeatedly playing “Only You” – eventually, their minds associated the song with an irresistible urge to obey Jacob’s kill order​. Thus, whenever Jacob broadcast that song over loudspeakers, his sleeper agents (unknowingly programmed) would snap and carry out violent tasks. The Junior Deputy themselves fell victim: after being Jacob’s prisoner, the Deputy would fly into a involuntary frenzy at the sound, compelled to complete a timed gauntlet and ultimately made to murder Eli Palmer under its influenc​e. 

This method was Jacob’s twisted way of “culling the herd” – using the enemy against themselves. In-universe, the Resistance came to fear that melody; hearing its opening bars echo in the pines made seasoned fighters drop to cover their ears, knowing something bad was about to happen. It turned a sweet 1950s love song into a weapon of horror. Jacob essentially proved Pavlovian conditioning could create Manchurian candidates.

entries.name: Prepper Stashes
entries.content:
Hope County had a long history of doomsday preppers and that only intensified under Eden’s Gate. The landscape is riddled with bunkers and caches stockpiled with food, weapons, and supplies for “the Collapse.” Many locals, even those not in the cult, built hidden stashes – fallout shelters under their backyards, caves sealed off with secret codes, etc. During the cult’s rise, Joseph either co-opted or destroyed independent bunkers (he gave people a choice: join his Project and share your bunker, or be deemed a heretic and lose it). As a result, the cult greatly bolstered its armory by absorbing these prepper stashes. For the Resistance and Deputy, these same bunkers became treasure troves – numerous times, they located a prepper hatch (marked often by a yellow paint splash or a note) and accessed it to find much-needed ammo or gear. In-world, people spread rumors like “I hear old man Briar’s bunker by the river still has a working generator and medical kits.” Such tips were gold for those surviving off the land.

Mechanics of Bunker Life: Inside these bunkers, whether cult or independent, you’d find hydroponic gardens, stockpiles of MREs (meal rations), water filtration systems, and of course, weapons caches. One ubiquitous item was the prepper code lock – many stashes had puzzles or requirements to open (to keep out uninitiated). In lore, a prepper might rig their bunker door to only open if you shoot a hidden switch, or only during a certain time of day, etc., to ensure privacy. These quirks became local legends. The Resistance ended up publishing a makeshift “Survival Guide” listing known bunker locations and how to access them, effectively turning Eden’s Gate’s own prep into a scavenger hunt for freedom fighters.

entries.name: Cult Bunkers
entries.content: Eden’s Gate itself constructed large bunkers, especially at key compounds. Each Herald oversaw a major bunker: John had an underground silo complex where he imprisoned and “atoned” sinners (when the Deputy raided it to rescue Hudson, they found rows of cells and torture chambers – a literal hell beneath the farmlands). Jacob utilized an old Cold War missile bunker high in the Whitetails (the cult converted it into an ammunition depot and training facility; that bunker later served as a refuge for Whitetail militia after Jacob’s fall). Faith’s region featured hidden catacombs beneath the broken Joseph statue and at an abandoned brewery – these acted as chemical labs for Bliss. And at Joseph’s island, there’s a central bunker system (including Dutch’s bunker, later used by Joseph). The cult taught its followers that these bunkers were “arks” – sanctuaries for the worthy when Collapse comes. Many civilians were forcibly herded into some cult bunkers “for their protection,” which often meant imprisonment.

entries.name: Dutch’s Bunker
entries.content: Dutch’s bunker on Dutch’s Island, which started as one man’s paranoid shelter, ended up housing the Deputy and Joseph Seed in the final moments of the Collapse. Dutch had everything: radio equipment (through which he guided the Deputy initially), CCTV monitors watching cult roadblocks, and a personal journal chronicling the slow invasion of Hope County.
